summary: All five AC criteria confirmed met by source inspection. The refactor is architecturally sound, correct, and clean.
FetchCache::__construct($cacheFolderPath): parameter name is expressive, rtrim() is a good defensive measure, docblock accurately describes the no-append semantics.

Comic::getCacheFolder() correctly returns getStorageFolder() . '/cache', anchoring the cache inside downloaded/ — this is the key bug fix (previously getFolder() was used, placing cache outside the storage hierarchy).
Fetcher::__construct() now delegates cache-folder knowledge to Comic::getCacheFolder() rather than constructing the path itself — clean single-responsibility improvement.
Test factories in both test files correctly mirror the real Comic semantics: FetchCache is given the already-suffixed '/cache' path directly.
All 58 tests pass; PHPStan clean on all 5 modified files.

comments.note: FetchCacheTests.php hardcodes the manifest path as $this->tempDir . '/cache/cache-manifest.json' in the helper method, duplicating the internal path logic of FetchCache. A public FetchCache::getManifestPath() getter would let the test reference it authoritatively. Pre-existing test pattern, not introduced by this WP; low priority.

FetchCache::put() writes the HTML file with file_put_contents(), which is not atomic (unlike the manifest which uses JSONFile::putData() via a temp-file rename). A write failure mid-way could leave a truncated HTML file with a valid manifest entry. Pre-existing issue, not in scope for this WP.
